extracted.intended_audience: Prospective CHI 2024 paper authors (researchers and practitioners in HCI preparing conference submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and acceptance criteria for preparing and submitting Papers to the CHI 2024 conference, including formatting, anonymization, ethics, supplementary materials, and presentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / No concurrent publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be original; it cannot be published or under concurrent review elsewhere. If you make multiple submissions to CHI 2024 Papers, they must be distinct from each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your submission is built directly on work currently under review at other venues, include an anonymized version in the concurrent submissions field; follow the ACM guide on prior and simultaneous submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limits and proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Short Papers: Submissions of 5,000 words or less are strongly encouraged. Standard Length Papers: Submissions between 5000 and 12000 words are considered standard. Submissions of 12,000 words or more will be considered excessively long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to submit a paper of length proportional to its contribution. Submissions above 12,000 words will receive extra scrutiny for whether the contribution is commensurate with length and could be desk rejected. Papers where length is incommensurate with contributions will be desk rejected. Short papers are recognised as short submissions and reviewers should match evaluation expectations to length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template / Review format
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure that you use the correct template; a single-column format must be used for the reviewing phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ACM SIGCHI Proceedings Format template. Use of different templates or formats may result in desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be anonymized; please ensure that your submission conforms to the Anonymization Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that violate the anonymization policy, including within the supplemental materials or external links to datasets, code repositories, etc., will be desk rejected. All video and supplementary material must be anonymized; non-anonymized supplemental materials will result in desk rejection of the entire submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata integrity and author list rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All submission metadata, including required fields in PCS like author names, affiliations, and order, must be complete and correct by the submission deadline. No changes to metadata after the submission deadline will be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract deadline: title, abstract, authors, subcommittee choices, and other metadata must be submitted before the abstract deadline; only the contact author can edit submission files after the abstract deadline. Placeholder metadata are not acceptable. Listed authors cannot be changed after the abstract deadline; no new authors can be added during revisions or for camera-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research quality / sufficiency of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must include enough detail that the research can be reviewed for research quality, given the norms and expectations of the relevant subcommittee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design papers will be judged by expectations of the design community, not by other communities. Papers that do not include enough detail to adequately assess research quality may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and supplementary materials encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, authors are strongly encouraged to provide supplementary materials to support practices around research reproducibility as much as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include survey text, experimental protocols, source code, and data. Any non-video supplementary material should be submitted as a single .zip file including a README describing the materials. Reviewers should be able to access the contribution of the paper solely based on the main submission file; the paper must stand on its own without the supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper submissions are expected to follow the SIGCHI Guide to an Accessible Submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessible submissions are essential for reviewers and are good practice. If you have questions contact the Accessibility Chairs early. Papers flagged as inaccessible by a reviewer will have to be reassigned; inaccessible submissions may limit reviewer matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper authors should pay careful attention to who is – and is not – included in their submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use gender-inclusive language and consider what communities their work is and is not supporting, and their geographical context. Where inclusivity is not possible, it should be acknowledged. See HCI Guidelines for Gender Equity and Inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent submissions / related-work disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any concurrent submissions to CHI that are closely related – i.e., are based on the same study, artefact, or dataset – you must include an anonymized version of that submission to the concurrent submissions field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same rule applies if your submission is built directly on work currently under review at other venues. See ACM guide on prior and simultaneous submissions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM (large language model) usage disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Text generated from a large-scale language model (LLM) such as ChatGPT must be clearly marked where such tools are used for purposes beyond editing the author's own text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee will not be using tools to detect LLM-generated text but will investigate submissions brought to their attention and may desk reject papers where LLM use is not clearly marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary video guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Video figures: Video figures do not have a specified time limit, although staying within 5 minutes is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details are available in the Guide to Submitting a Video. Authors must also upload a 30-second optional preview for accepted papers and a mandatory up-to-15-minute video presentation by the video presentation deadline for accepted authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material format and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Other supplementary material (e.g., survey text, protocols, source code, data) should be submitted as a single .zip file including a README.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary materials must be anonymized. Reviewers should be able to understand the paper without accessing supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission completeness and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must submit title, abstract, authors, subcommittee selections, and other metadata by the abstract deadline; main paper pdf and related form data must be submitted before the main paper deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new submissions will be allowed after the abstract deadline. Any submissions showing 'incomplete' after the main paper deadline will be deleted. Video and supplementary material have separate deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittee selection responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When you submit a paper, you can state a preference of up to two subcommittees whose mandates you believe your topic fits into.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the authors' responsibility to select subcommittees that offer the best expertise to assess the research. The program committee may reassign submissions if neither selected subcommittee possesses adequate expertise. If unsure, email subcommittee chairs for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and resubmit phase
rubrics_metrics.description: CHI 2024 Papers will continue with a revise and resubmit phase for papers above a certain threshold, allowing authors to respond to reviewer feedback and improve their paper as part of the review cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should read the rationale post by the paper chairs and follow the described revise/resubmit process and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirement for accepted authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted manuscripts require presentation at the CHI Conference; accepted authors are not required to travel but must present synchronously in-person or asynchronously remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All accepted authors are required to upload a video presentation of up to 15 minutes by the video presentation deadline. Failure to participate in presenting may result in withdrawal from the ACM Digital Library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication-ready and camera-ready requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact authors of accepted papers will receive instructions to prepare and submit a final version by the Publication-Ready Deadline; publications must follow the new LaTeX and Word ACM templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors are unable to meet these requirements the Papers Chairs may be notified and the paper may be removed from the program. Technical questions go to publications@chi2024.acm.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright / Open Access and permissions responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be required to assign either copyright or license to the ACM or to pay a fee to ACM for Open Access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility for obtaining permissions to use video, audio, or pictures of identifiable people or proprietary content rests with the author, not ACM or CHI. See ACM rights management links provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official publication date and patent considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The official publication date is the date the proceedings are made available in the ACM Digital Library and may be up to two weeks prior to the first day of the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This date may affect patent filing deadlines related to published work. The official publication date may remain the first day of the conference even in special cases noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary review acceptance criteria (evaluation dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will excel in originality, significance, validity, reproducibility, and presentation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHI Papers are judged for broad impact on HCI theory, method, and practice across academia and industry. Reviewers and PC consider these dimensions when recommending acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk-rejection causes and screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may be desk rejected for reasons including non-anonymization, excessive length without commensurate contribution, placeholder/incomplete submissions, or clearly not being complete research papers (e.g., abstracts, WIPs, entire theses, extensive journal articles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure that their submission conforms to policies, templates, and completeness requirements to avoid desk rejection.
